# How to annotate {#sec-how-to-annotate}

This script supports collaborative annotation with
[Hypothesis](https://web.hypothes.is/): highlight any passage and attach a
comment directly to it.

## Join the course group first

Annotations for this course live in the private group **IKT 448 2026**,
not in the Public layer:

1. Create a free account at [hypothes.is](https://hypothes.is/signup) if
   you do not have one.
2. Open the group page -
   [hypothes.is/groups/XjreopNx/ikt-448-2026](https://hypothes.is/groups/XjreopNx/ikt-448-2026) -
   and click **Join group** (you must be signed in).
3. On any page of this script, open the Hypothesis sidebar and switch the
   scope selector at the top from *Public* to **IKT 448 2026** before you
   post. Check the selector each session - the client remembers it per
   browser, not per site.

Annotations posted in the group are visible to group members only; anything
posted to *Public* is world-readable and does **not** count for the course.

::: {.content-visible unless-meta="annotations"}
::: {.callout-warning}

## What counts as a substantive annotation

Annotations are graded on substance, not volume. Three kinds count:

- **Question** - a genuine question about the passage that a fellow student
  could learn from seeing answered. "I don't get this" does not count;
  "does X also hold when Y, given what @sec- says about Z?" does.
- **Correction** - a factual, technical, or editorial error in the text,
  with a short justification and, where relevant, a source.
- **Practice example** - a concrete, worked example, counter-example, or
  real-world case that illustrates the passage, described precisely enough
  that it could be merged into the script.

Not substantive: "+1"/agreement notes, restating the text, formatting
complaints without a fix, or duplicating an existing annotation (read the
thread first).

## Per-chapter quota

> **Placeholder - to be confirmed with the course setup:** *N* substantive
> annotations per student per chapter (planned: 2), counted per the rules
> above. Annotations on any chapter count; spreading them across chapters
> is encouraged but not required.

## How annotations get merged into the script

1. At the end of each teaching block, annotations are triaged by the course
   lead. Substantive ones are turned into an edit: corrections are applied,
   good questions become clarified text or an FAQ box, practice examples
   become worked examples or exercise scenarios.
2. Merged contributions are **credited in `CHANGELOG.md`** - one line per
   merged contribution, naming the contributor (or their chosen handle) and
   the chapter/section changed.
3. Larger contributions (a full worked example, a new exercise scenario, a
   glossary entry) follow the co-authorship flow in `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
   including its review rubric and licence statement.

Your annotation remains yours in Hypothesis; the merged text becomes part of
the script under the script's licence (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
